claims.statement: entrypoint.py is the composition root: build_supervisor consumes process secrets into a RuntimeConfig and composes SandboxSupervisor with RepositoryBoot (plus TunnelEnvironment, RepositoryHooks, RepositorySynchronizer), ManagedSkillsMaterializer (only when a control-plane URL and session id exist), OpenCodeServer, AgentBridgeProcess, CodeServer, WebTerminal, and BrowserDesktop; SIGTERM/SIGINT are routed to supervisor.request_shutdown which only sets the supervisor-owned asyncio.Event.

SandboxSupervisor.run enforces boot ordering: tunnel preparation, BUILD short-circuit (image-build execution under OI_IMAGE_BUILD_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS with provider success/failure callbacks), best-effort BrowserDesktop start, RepositoryBoot.boot, managed-skills materialization (after repo boot so OpenCode restarts reuse the tree), best-effort code-server and web-terminal starts, then fatal OpenCode start and bridge start, and finally the monitor loop; shutdown stops services in reverse order.

BootMode has four values (FRESH, SNAPSHOT_RESTORE, REPO_IMAGE, BUILD) resolved from the environment (IMAGE_BUILD_MODE / RESTORED_FROM_SNAPSHOT / FROM_REPO_IMAGE), and the supervisor re-exports the resolved mode as OPENINSPECT_BOOT_MODE so repository hook scripts can branch on it.

monitor_processes applies an explicit per-service restart policy bounded by MAX_RESTARTS=5 with exponential backoff (base 2, capped at 60 s): OpenCode and bridge crashes are restarted and become fatal (control-plane error report plus shutdown) at the limit; a bridge exit code 0 is a graceful exit that shuts the sandbox down; code-server, web-terminal, and browser-desktop restarts are best-effort and never kill the session.

Fatal supervisor errors are POSTed to {control_plane}/sessions/{session_id}/sandbox-error with fatal:true, the last 1000 characters, a Bearer sandbox token, and the X-Sandbox-ID header, using up to 3 attempts with 2^n-second backoff; reporting failures are logged but never crash the supervisor.

RepositoryBoot parses repositories once via repo_config.parse_repositories: repo owners are validated as namespace paths by is_safe_repo_owner (slash-joined safe segments, enabling GitLab subgroups), names must be single safe path segments and are unique case-insensitively because checkouts are /workspace/<name>, and a validation violation is treated as a corrupt/tampered config that fails boot immediately.

The supervisor writes the canonical repository manifest to /tmp/oi-repo-manifest.json before and after sync ({owner, name, branch, path, baseSha?} per entry); the bridge's push targeting and the JS create-pull-request tool read that manifest instead of re-deriving /workspace paths, making it the single authority for the checkout layout.

RepositoryBoot.boot applies strictness by boot mode: git-sync failures are fatal in FRESH and BUILD (raising RuntimeError naming the timed-out and failed repos) but only produce boot warnings on SNAPSHOT_RESTORE/REPO_IMAGE; setup.sh runs only for FRESH and BUILD (fatal in BUILD, warning otherwise); start.sh runs in every non-BUILD mode after the tunnel wait, and a start.sh failure in the first (primary) repository is fatal while later repositories only warn.

Repository hooks execute .openinspect/setup.sh and .openinspect/start.sh in each checkout via bash with merged stdout/stderr, timeouts from SETUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 300) and START_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 120) with silent fallback on unparseable values, process-group termination on timeout, the last 50 output lines logged in non-build modes, and OPENINSPECT_BOOT_MODE injected into the script environment; missing scripts count as success.

TunnelEnvironment implements the tunnel-env wait logic: EXPECTED_TUNNEL_PORTS is parsed as a comma-separated port list, clear_stale_file deletes /workspace/.tunnels.env unless its TUNNEL_SANDBOX_ID marker matches the current sandbox (the manager's write can land before the entrypoint starts), and wait_until_ready polls every 0.2 s up to TUNNEL_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 30) for a TUNNEL_<port>= line per expected port, warning rather than failing on timeout.

OpenCodeServer starts `opencode serve --port 4096 --hostname 0.0.0.0 --print-logs` in the workdir (the single repo checkout when it exists with .git, otherwise /workspace), configures it via OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT with {provider}/{model}, blanket allow permissions, and session MCP servers, sets OPENCODE_CLIENT=serve to disable the interactive question tool, and polls /global/health for up to 30 seconds.

Before launching OpenCode, the server stages the filesystem: multi-repo .opencode/ assembly (position order, later repos win with warnings, node_modules preserved), agent tools copied into .opencode/tool/ (inspect-plugin.js as create-pull-request.js for repository sessions; slack-notify.js gated on AGENT_SLACK_NOTIFY_ENABLED), plugin dependency seeding from /app/opencode-deps to avoid an arborist reify on the first request, bundled skills copied into .opencode/skills/, standalone bin CLIs installed outside .opencode/tool/ to avoid tool-discovery execution, managed OAuth sentinels written to ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json (0600, atomic rename), npx MCP packages pre-installed with a 180-second budget, and runtime-installed paths registered in .git/info/exclude.

The AgentBridge connects to {control_plane}/sessions/{session_id}/ws?type=sandbox with Bearer sandbox-token and X-Sandbox-ID headers, sends a ready event carrying the sandbox id, OpenCode session id, SANDBOX_VERSION runtime version, and per-repository position/identity/base SHA from the manifest, drains the supervisor's boot-warnings file exactly once as warning events, and heartbeats every 30 seconds.

Bridge reconnection distinguishes transient from terminal failures: websockets.InvalidStatus with HTTP 401/403/404/410 raises SessionTerminatedError for a graceful exit; non-retryable GitSigningError or connection errors containing those HTTP statuses are fatal; anything else reconnects with exponential backoff (base 2 s, max 60 s), and per-connection metrics (connection count, reconnect attempts, total connected duration) are logged on disconnect with warn level for unexpected close codes.

BufferedEventForwarder owns reconnect-safe delivery: events are stamped with sandboxId/timestamp; five critical types (execution_complete, error, snapshot_ready, push_complete, push_error) carry deterministic ackIds and stay pending until the control plane's ack command; when unbound or failed, events buffer up to 1000 with oldest-non-critical eviction; bind flushes the buffer and re-sends still-pending criticals under one recovery lock with 30-second send timeouts so a wedged socket cannot wedge recovery.

_handle_command dispatches prompt, stop, snapshot, shutdown, git_sync_complete, push, refresh_diff, and ack; prompt tasks are deliberately NOT returned to the WebSocket listener (which cancels background tasks on disconnect) so prompts survive WS disconnects, and a done-callback releases the diff worker's idle gate, emits execution_complete on cancellation/exception, and triggers a session diff refresh on success.

_handle_prompt parses the control-plane-selected Git author (agent-only → None, attributed-user requires explicit non-empty name/email, anything else raises GitSigningError), ensures a validated OpenCode session persisted at /tmp/opencode-session-id, hydrates attachments with invalid ones skipped via user-facing warnings, streams via OpenCodePromptStream, always terminates with execution_complete, and treats a prompt that emitted no output as an error rather than silent success.

Stop cancels the current prompt task and best-effort aborts the OpenCode session to save LLM compute; shutdown cancels the prompt and sets the bridge shutdown event; snapshot replies snapshot_ready with the OpenCode session id; prompt max duration derives from SANDBOX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 7200) minus a snapshot reserve of min(900, 25%), and BRIDGE_SSE_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT (default 120 s, clamped to 5–3600) invalid and out-of-range values are clamped with warnings rather than crashing.

OpenCodePromptStream achieves attribution by construction: it generates an OpenCode-compatible ascending user-message id (OpenCodeIdentifier.ascending) sent as the prompt's messageID so OpenCode stamps assistant messages with parentID pointing at it; MessageAttribution accepts only this prompt's output, the compaction fallback orders by time.created rather than id comparison because the 48-bit-truncated ids wrap every ~795 days, and a prompt deadline plus SSE inactivity deadline guard the stream loop with request_stop and final-state fetch on timeout paths.

The SSE translator maps OpenCode events to bridge events: session.created and task-tool metadata register child sessions correlated by call id; session.updated forwards a changed session title once (default titles suppressed); message.updated authorizes assistant messages and drains pending parts (cap 2000); message.part.updated becomes token (cumulative text), tool_call (deduplicated per tool/session/call/status), or step_start/step_finish; child text is never forwarded and child tool/error events carry isSubtask, childSessionId, and taskCallId; only parent-session idle terminates the stream, after which final message state is fetched to emit any text longer than what was streamed.

Parent session.error emits one deduplicated error event and fails the stream, except ContextOverflowError which announces automatic compaction and is swallowed: session.compacted emits context_compacted and clears the pending error, and if the session goes idle with neither compaction nor an emitted error, the original overflow is surfaced instead of reporting silent success; child-session overflow is always swallowed and child errors never end the stream.

The prompt request body maps model to providerID/modelID (bare names default to anthropic) and reasoningEffort per provider: Anthropic adaptive-thinking models get thinking adaptive plus outputConfig.effort, other Anthropic models get thinking budgetTokens (high 16000, max 31999), OpenAI gets reasoningEffort plus reasoningSummary auto, and xAI passes the effort as a request variant; the OpenCodeClient owns the wire (prompt_async, /event SSE with inactivity deadline, abort, message fetch) and translates transport failures mid-stream into SSEConnectionError after preserving partial output via final-state fetch.

The push command normalizes a provider-generated pushSpec into a PushRequest (targetBranch, repoOwner, repoName, refspec, remoteUrl, redactedRemoteUrl, force; absent fields normalize to empty/False), rejects a missing spec, partial repo identity, missing branch, or missing refspec/URL as PushRejected; checkout resolution matches owner/name case-insensitively against the supervisor manifest and uses the matched entry's path verbatim (spec strings never become filesystem paths), falling back to the sole checkout directly under /workspace when no identity is given.

git push runs with a 300-second timeout and terminate-then-kill after a 5-second grace; stderr is redacted by replacing the push URL with its redacted counterpart and rewriting https://user@ to https://***@; the terminal push_complete and push_error events always include branchName (so the control plane can resolve a pending push) and echo repoOwner/repoName when the spec carried them.

GitSigningRuntime.refresh fetches /sessions/{id}/commit-signing and applies per-repository local git config across every manifest repository: with signing disabled it sets the prompt author (or OpenInspect <open-inspect@noreply.github.com>) as author/committer and removes prior signing config; with SSH signing enabled it sets gpg.format=ssh, gpg.ssh.program to the installed oi-git-sign CLI, user.signingkey=key::<ed25519 public key>, commit.gpgsign=true, the control-plane committer identity, and the prompt author (or configured committer) as author; a non-retryable signing failure at bridge startup is fatal while retryable ones (408/429/5xx) ride the reconnect loop.

oi-git-sign (git_signer.py) is a stateless SSH signing proxy: it validates git's -Y sign invocation, reads a bounded commit payload, POSTs it to /sessions/{id}/commit-signing with a key-fingerprint header, validates the armored response, and atomically writes the signature file, with errors that never contain request, response, or credential bytes.

The git credential helper serves SCM credentials only for protocol=https and host equal to VCS_HOST (default github.com), exiting 0 with no output otherwise so git falls through without ever emitting the token to a plaintext or foreign-host remote; it mints fresh credentials via POST /sessions/{session_id}/scm-credentials, caches them at /run/oi/scm-creds.json (0600) until within a 5-minute expiry buffer with advisory-flock serialization and a post-lock recheck, never uses the cache as a fallback for a failed refresh, and refuses the VCS_CLONE_TOKEN fallback when control-plane env is present but incomplete; store/erase are no-ops.

Image-build sandboxes without control-plane context authenticate via the injected VCS_CLONE_TOKEN (username VCS_CLONE_USERNAME or x-access-token) treated as valid for one hour; the gh CLI wrapper at /usr/local/bin/gh execs the real gh with a freshly minted token from the helper's gh-token action only when the environment has nothing usable (never overriding GH_TOKEN, refreshing only the OI_GITHUB_TOKEN_IS_FALLBACK=1 system fallback, never minting for non-github deployments), and a failed mint prints nothing so the wrapper falls back to the ambient environment.

ManagedSkillsClient pages GET /sessions/{session_id}/sandbox-skills at 50 skills per request with cursor pagination, streams responses under a 32 MiB cap, and retries retryable failures (408/429/5xx, transport errors) up to 3 times with exponential backoff from 0.25 s.

validate_installation_page treats managed-skills bytes as untrusted and enforces materializer limits before any content reaches a discovery path: schema version 1; SHA-256 manifest id with every page pinned to the first page's; skill names ≤64 chars matching ^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$ and globally unique; ≤100 files per skill; file content ≤256 KiB with sizeBytes matching and SHA-256 verified; ≤1 MiB per-skill revisions and ≤5 MiB whole-install content; paths ≤240 UTF-8 bytes, depth ≤10, no absolutes/traversal/backslashes/control characters/file-directory conflicts; executable only under scripts/; a required SKILL.md whose frontmatter name matches the managed name; and non-final pages must be non-empty so paging always terminates.

ManagedSkillsMaterializer.materialize installs through a crash-safe swap: stage into .managed-skills-staging with O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW files at mode 0500/0400 that are fsynced and hash-re-verified on disk, write the swap journal before moving the current tree to .managed-skills-backup, rename staging into place, then clean up; _repair_interrupted_swap restores the last complete tree after an interrupted swap, and managed names colliding with already-discovered skills (bundled skills, workspace or member .opencode/skills, .claude/skills, .agents/skills, home-directory equivalents) are dropped with a warning so repo-local skills keep precedence.

The sandbox ships the child-session tool family and slack-notify, all authenticated against the control plane via _bridge-client.js (session id from SESSION_CONFIG, Bearer SANDBOX_AUTH_TOKEN): spawn-child POSTs /children (restricted by description to explicit child-session requests, distinct from in-process Task delegation; 403/429 mapped to guidance), send-child-prompt POSTs /children/{id}/prompt to queue follow-ups, get-child-status lists children or fetches details with includeResponse and paginated trajectory, cancel-child POSTs /children/{id}/cancel with cancelNested defaulting to true; underscore-prefixed helper files are shared modules, not tools; slack-notify POSTs /slack-notify and returns structured failure envelopes with a stable reason-to-guidance map including delivery_unknown no-auto-retry guidance.

provider-token-broker.js implements a provider-neutral single-flight token broker that POSTs /sessions/{id}/provider-auth/{provider}/access-token, caches results with a 5-minute refresh buffer, and validates the response shape; codex-auth-plugin.js overrides OpenCode's built-in Codex auth so rotating OpenAI refresh tokens persist in the control plane rather than dying with the sandbox (model allow-list, injected GPT 5.3 Codex entries, zeroed costs, local auth-state rewrite on refresh), and xai-auth-plugin.js keeps SuperGrok refresh tokens control-plane-side, injects the grok-build-0.1 model, and wraps fetch to attach the brokered short-lived access token.

Auxiliary services are capability-gated: CodeServer starts only with CODE_SERVER_PASSWORD (code-server --auth password on 0.0.0.0:{CODE_SERVER_PORT}, default 8080); WebTerminal starts only with TERMINAL_ENABLED (ttyd writable bash on localhost:7681 with 5-second readiness wait, then the Bun ttyd_proxy on TTYD_PROXY_PORT default 7680, ttyd never exposed); BrowserDesktop starts only with VNC_PASSWORD (Xvfb on :1 1280x720x24 without TCP listeners, fluxbox, x11vnc on localhost:5900 with a 3DES password file capped at 8 bytes, websockify/noVNC on 0.0.0.0:{NOVNC_PORT} default 6080); every child process runs with merged stdout/stderr forwarded into the structured log.

In image-build mode the entrypoint implements Modal's create-bind-launch protocol: run_modal_image_build waits (shutdown-aware) for one 64-hex callback token on stdin after sandbox binding, validates length/encoding/format, builds a RepoImageBuildCallback from the build-id/callback env vars which are then popped, and runs repository boot in BUILD mode under the execution timeout, reporting report_success (build duration, repository SHAs, SANDBOX_VERSION) or report_failure through the callback before idling until shutdown; image builds have no live session, so sync and setup failures are fatal and start.sh does not run.

RepositorySynchronizer clones missing checkouts (depth 100, 300-second clone timeout) and updates existing ones (120-second fetch timeout) in parallel, resetting origin to a plain HTTPS URL and fetching/checking out the base branch except on SNAPSHOT_RESTORE where the restored working tree is preserved, returns per-repo SUCCEEDED/FAILED/TIMED_OUT outcomes, and resolves session diff baselines after sync.

AgentBridgeProcess launches the bridge as `python -m sandbox_runtime.bridge` with --sandbox-id/--session-id/--control-plane/--token/--opencode-port when a control-plane URL and session id exist (skipping otherwise), forwards its logs, and flags a startup crash after 0.5 seconds; the SessionDiffRefreshWorker coalesces terminal prompt executions into one eventual idle checkout refresh uploaded to the control plane's session diff endpoints, treating a 404 as an unsupported control plane and stopping uploads for the sandbox's life.
